layers.evidence_basis: NASA PGDA product 78 provides a nominal 5 m raster but states that roughly 90% of the polar LDEM pixels are interpolated. LL-009Q can quantify the published clone ensemble at raster support points, but neither nominal 5 m spacing nor the clone ensemble is a theorem that continuous terrain between support points is bounded.

NASA PGDA product 90 provides an 80 m elevation COG and a colocated effective-resolution raster. Effective-resolution evidence can qualify which samples are admitted, but it is not by itself a deterministic upper bound on unresolved terrain between samples.

expected_result_before_further_closure.risk_qualified_horizon: blocked while any admitted layer is sample_points_only or unknown
expected_result_before_further_closure.empirical_sampled_horizon: allowed only with explicit sample-support disclosure and no unknown layer
expected_result_before_further_closure.descriptive_only: allowed with explicit per-layer support classes

nested_resolution_policy.purpose: Measure observed positive skyline excursions that appear in finer exact terrain but are absent from a coarser exact terrain layer over the same configured overlap.

candidate_follow_on_evidence: Exact nested 5 m/20 m/40 m/80 m elevation comparisons where coverage overlaps
PGDA effective-resolution maps as admission/qualification evidence
PGDA multi-baseline RMSD/roughness/Hurst products as empirical spatial-structure evidence after source-methodology review
A source-supported deterministic gradient/Lipschitz theorem, if one can actually be established
Independent higher-resolution terrain such as validated SfS products where licensing/provenance permits evidence use
non_claims: Nominal pixel spacing is not a continuous-terrain upper bound.
Effective resolution is not relabeled as a Lipschitz or interpolation theorem.
Sampled slope, RMS roughness and Hurst exponent are not deterministic local gradient bounds unless their source methodology explicitly supports that interpretation.
Spatial-support semantics are independent of LL-009O/Q vertical-error and ensemble uncertainty semantics.
